title: Millisecond optical coherence and strong collective coupling in an integrated telecom rare-earth photonic platform
authors: Kah Jen Wo, Pavel A. Dmitriev, Karthik Dasigi, Fumiya Hanamura, Steven Touzard
abstract: Long-range quantum network nodes require the combination of strong light-matter coupling, long coherence times and in situ spectral control at telecom wavelengths. The coherence of erbium in integrated devices is held back by its hosts, which do not simultaneously provide the weakly magnetic nuclear-spin environment and the well-defined substitutional sites found in coherence-optimised bulk crystals. Here we bring such an optimised crystal onto a photonic chip, by bonding an Er${^{3+}}$:CaWO${_{4}}$ host without an adhesive interlayer to a high-${Q}$ electro-optically tuneable thin-film lithium niobate microring resonator. At an effective temperature of ${75}$ mK and a field of only ${0.2}$ T, the bonded ensemble retains an effective homogeneous linewidth of ${289\pm34}$ Hz (${T_\text{M}=1.10\pm0.13}$ ms), with spectral diffusion proceeding at ${86\pm18}$ Hz and saturating at ${1.5\pm0.2}$ kHz. Electro-optically tuning the resonator through the erbium optical transition resolves an avoided crossing with a collective cooperativity of ${C=6.7\pm0.4}$. Exploiting superhyperfine coupling to the host's ${^{183}}$W nuclear spins, we store and retrieve optical phase information over ${5}$ s with a visibility of ${0.935\pm0.015}$. Strong collective coupling, millisecond coherence and in situ spectral tuning in a single device thus establish heterogeneous integration leveraging coherence-optimised hosts as a route to scalable telecom quantum networks.
summary: The researchers engineered a novel photonic platform by bonding an optimized $	ext{Er}^{3+}:	ext{CaWO}_4$ crystal onto a tunable lithium niobate resonator. They achieved millisecond optical coherence and strong light-matter coupling, while also demonstrating long-term quantum phase storage mediated by host nuclear spins. This integration proves a scalable architecture for future telecom quantum networks.
main_problem: Developing scalable quantum network nodes requires combining strong light-matter coupling, long coherence times, and in situ spectral control at telecom wavelengths.
main_result: The integrated device successfully demonstrates strong collective coupling, millisecond optical coherence, and tunable spectral properties, establishing a viable route for scalable telecom quantum networks.
method: The study uses three-pulse photon echo (3PPE) techniques to measure coherence and spectral diffusion, alongside electro-optic tuning measurements to characterize light-matter interaction strength.
model_or_system: The platform is a heterogeneously integrated system combining an optimized $	ext{Er}^{3+}:	ext{CaWO}_4$ crystal with a high-$	ext{Q}$, electro-optically tuneable thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) microring resonator.
key_observables: Effective homogeneous linewidth ($\Gamma_{	ext{eff}}$), spectral diffusion rate ($\Gamma_{SD}$), collective cooperativity ($C$), and optical phase storage visibility ($V$).
important_parameters: Coherence time ($T_	ext{M}$) of $1.10 \pm 0.13	ext{ms}$; strong coupling constant $C=6.7 \pm 0.4$; phase storage time up to $5$ seconds.
main_assumptions: The success relies on the optimized $	ext{Er}^{3+}:	ext{CaWO}_4$ host providing a weakly magnetic environment and well-defined sites, overcoming limitations of previous doping methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the integrated platform, coherence measurements using 3PPE showing linewidth evolution, and transmission spectra demonstrating avoided crossings related to strong coupling.
paper_structure: The paper details the necessity for advanced quantum nodes, presents the novel heterogeneously integrated platform, reports quantitative measurements of coherence (linewidth/diffusion), demonstrates strong coupling via tuning, and finally showcases long-lived phase storage using nuclear spins.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses key engineering challenges in solid-state quantum memory by integrating high-coherence rare-earth systems into scalable photonic circuits for quantum networking applications.
